Question: I’m 25 and I feel like I cannot add anything to a conversation or start a conversation of interest or even understand what anyone is saying. Could it be depression? If so what could I do to train my mind?

If you’re depressed, it’s because you have a problem conversing with others and you don’t know how to overcome it. You are suffering from the common anxiety of fear of sounding goofy. It takes practice to train your voice and make your presentation trustworthy. When I was a kid, I wanted to be better at talking to people. I would stand in front of a big mirror when I was alone and practice reading, telling jokes, lying, whatever. The result was that I could look and sound confident and sincere no matter what I was thinking or how scared I was on the inside. I taught myself what is taught in speech classes. I practiced voice tones, facial expressions, body language, and looking into my eyes in the mirror until I could say anything to anybody without any anxiety. I became “silver-tongued,” meaning that I could speak exceptionally clearly and well. And I have spent the majority of my working life doing most people’s worst fear — public speaking. Do it. Practice, practice, practice when you’re alone. Sing along with your favorites. Read stories aloud with feeling and expressing emotions. Have conversations with yourself, pretending you are in different settings and subjects. You can do this and it will work!

Question: Should I take my 17-year-old’s phone at night?

Question: When at a social event and wanting to make a new friend, is it better to wait for others to introduce themselves first or introduce yourself first ?

After all, you already think of them as “friend quality” or you wouldn’t be wanting to meet them — right? Friends don’t do formal introductions every time they meet, so skip that for later. Try to make the connection when neither of you are distracted. Look for something good that the two of you can easily agree on. Are they wearing a team logo sweatshirt, driving a cool car, enduring the hot day, whatever? Then You Open with casually complimenting them on something or make small-talk with the same voice you would use with a good friend. The chances are good that they also want to be friendly. If I can make eye contact, I can usually get a conversation started, and So. Can. You! And if you hit a lull in the conversation, “Oh by the way, I’m Joe” first name-kind of introductions are a great way to start the relationship. Honestly, I’ve gotten into conversations with countless people this way, and then my wife would want to know who I was talking to and we had never exchanged names — but we parted as friends and not strangers.

Question: Can you imagine school without friends? What are the reasons and facts?
Answer: School isn’t about friendship. Yes, sure, its secondary purpose is to keep a bunch of kids busy while the rest of us are making a living. Some people work best on their own, but the social structure of most schools are designed to work best if students can learn how to get along, as friends to exchange helping. “How to get long” is taught by confining students in different groups and letting them learn how on their own. But its primary purpose is to transmit to those same kids, the basic knowledge and language skills to enable them to be self-supporting by the time they are eighteen. At that age, they need to produce as much or more than they consume. Friendships are nice, but learning how to afford one’s existence is vital. The average eighteen year-old usually feels they no longer need managing. So, it’s time for them to begin producing, their way.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why does he say he is looking for a partner but only wants to be friends with me but keeps talking about our past sex life?
Answer: It sounds to me like he is looking for a partner and he wants you to be friendly enough to provide him with sex on the side while he looks elsewhere. How does it feel to be considered a second-class slut? I think you’re better than that — don’t you? Tell him.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I handle two schoolmates who despise each other and try to get me on their side?
Answer: My lifelong First Rule of Friendship is: Nobody can tell me with who I can be friends. Not one friend against another, not my wife or any other relative. Nobody means nobody. I had two friends who hated each other. Both wanted me to dump the other one. I refused both, and stayed friends with both.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is the difference between a friend and an acquaintance? Can people have genuine friendships based solely on common interests?
Answer: An acquaintance is someone you recognize and possibly know their name, and with whom you may have semi-regular, brief contact. Think of a clerk at a store you frequent, a new kid on the block, your doctor, someone who works on the next work-station over from yours. A friend is someone you show you care for them, because they have shown they care for you. Usually there is a commonality which involves helping each other, and usually in frequent and close proximity. “The Servant Song” by Richard Gillard expresses it well. So does the Judeo/Christian Bible in the Book of Ecclesiastes, 4:9–12.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Can I get some agreement that the Facebook we used to know (where we'd see stuff from our actual friends) is long past? Except for life-changing events pretty much one's feed is short, random "eye candy" videos from Instagram influencers now?
Answer: That’s true for a lot of users, especially those who have not blocked or declined seeing the eye-candy and influencers. I’m active regularly on my personal site and several others. I’m an admin on a couple, and I’m a member on a couple that are so private nobody can even see them unless an existing member has already vetted them. Strictly one-interest, no junk, no nothing. Facebook offers a number of optional controls for who can land on your Fb page. In other words, if a lot of crap lands on your page, you left the door open for it to get there. And what you cannot stop, you can ignore.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is the best way to react to peevishness in a friend?
Answer: I try to avoid obnoxious and overly critical people.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What should I do? I'm 14 and have no real friends. All my "friends" don't care about me, invite me to parties, or even add me to the group chat. My lifelong best friend, who's not in the group, won't meet up in real life either. I feel lonely…
Answer: I am deeply sorry you have to endure your childhood through teenage years with — pardon my profane assessment — selfish brats and hateful little a$$holes. Of course you’re lonely because they are unsocial toward you. They think they in their little group are better than you are, and it makes them arrogant. They are the ones who will compete for the “mister cool and miss most beautiful” positions in high school. Remember their mistreatment, and whenever in high school or life after, they ask you for votes, favors, help or privileges of any kind, remind them about when they were hateful and selfish and shunned you. Tell them “not just no but never” unless they profusely apologize and show they mean it first. By the way, you’ll learn there is a whole crowd of others who have been similarly mistreated, and many of them will make great friends!

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do you accept that you're just meant to be a loner for life? I come from a narcissistic family, and after all the trauma, I'm tired of trying to go to events to make friends or meet partners because it never lasts. I just want to stop trying.
Answer: First, there’s no proof that you’re meant to be a loner for life. After my first wife filed for divorce, I prayed, “God, if you want me to marry again, please send me a woman who will be a faithful wife and a good mother to our children.” God did, and God did — but God didn’t want to waste such a fine partner on the jerk I was, so God put me through three years of becoming the male version before she would marry me, 47 years ago and counting. Second, the narcissistic family and the trauma is in the past so leave it there. Most of us have scars of some sort that fade with time and new experiences. A long-ago sales manager taught us, when we failed to close a deal to reach up and physically pretend we were flushing the bad experience down the toilet. Stop sitting in your family’s sh!t, find your symbolic way to flush it and move on. Third, “events to make friends or meet partners” can only cause you to gather with and become acquainted with other losers “because it never lasts.” Stop that waste of your life. You want a mate for a great rest-of your life. Make a list of what you enjoy or might enjoy doing where people are around and go there to do it. That’s how you find good “mate candidates” because you and they already have something to share. I met my first wife in a roller-skating rink. Two years after the divorce, I was a new Christian, and my now beloved mate was a Christian and invited me to her church. I bought a simple thumb-harp (about $30USD) and sometimes will sit on a public bench by a walkway playing with it. Friendly people will stop and ask about it, so right there I can get in a conversation and meet people. I’m a primitive-art craftsman and I make original necklaces, belt buckles, crosses and other small trinkets from deer antler, wood and shells. I wear my art and I get comments, thus meeting people who like what I do. Find your “fun hook” to start conversations and you’ll have much better chances to meet people you might want to know better.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can I navigate my friendships when I can tell they aren't strong anymore? 35 (F) My mom passed in January, none of them understand what it's like. I feel some pulling away, while others don't want to hear it anymore. Need advice.
Answer: In the first place, the 30’s life is when you should be your strongest. And your friends don’t want to hear about it because life is beginning to feel pretty good to them and they just don’t want to talk about that “death thing. That’s for old folks.” And they just aren’t ready for Death Happening. Death Happens, and Death Happens often when we’ve neglected the relationship and we have regrets. Death Happens tragically, often tearing apart families. Nobody wants to hear our “sob stories.” I suggest that you take up some physical activity. It stimulates good-feeling chemicals in your brain. If it’s on a treadmill or exercise machine, you can dialogue with yourself. You will feel better soon.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Would the average Australian make better friends with a Brit or an American?
Answer: I don’t have any experience or guidance to draw on… but always IMHO: The Brit, every time. It’s human, and it’s in their blood. Blood always tells and even if it was the ancestrial Brits that threw the original prisioners there, their since-then Aussie ancestry has hereditary connection to the property. In the South of America, we might hear, “Yeah, I been gone for a while, but I’ve got kinfolk back there.” And good friends count as close kin. Betcha.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Am I really draining my friend? My friend accidentally saw my self-harm scars during an argument and she told me to kill myself. What should I do? I am afraid of losing her because she's my friend.
Answer: No, you are mistaken. She is not your friend. Friends do not tell you to kill yourself. Nobody who has a history (I hope you quit cutting long ago) of self-harming should have people around them saying “kill yourself.”

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I want to hurt the person who has hurt me. Is it not rational and is rage filled?
Answer: In the Old Testament of the Judeo-Christian Bible, “an eye for an eye, tooth for tooth,” was considered fair and justice, for common injuries, while in Leviticus 19:18, God says don’t take revenge. In the New Testament, Jesus said that we should forgive seventy times seven, and in Romans 12:19, God says not to take revenge because God himself would do it for us. On that last idea about God providing vengance; many years ago, a man who had no real cause had me locked up in jail and it cost me what was a lot of money at the time. While I was plotting revenge, my biblically-literate mother-in-law pointed to the Romans verse and told me to tell God about it and let God do it. I gritted my teeth and did so, but I said I’d be watching to see if that was really true. In a very short time, that man suffered so much loss that I felt sorry for what I’d asked for, and I prayed God would stop. I was shocked when God answered that it wasn’t my choice when to stop but God’s. That man continued to lose everything — family, home, job, his health and died in misery with his son in jail. I’ve tried since then to not even think about revenge. I just try to forgive and move on, knowing that if it needs to be done, God will have seen it and I don’t want to see God’s vengeance on my account ever again.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Do you think that younger or older people have more friends? Why is this so?
Answer: I can give you a firm “Yes.” And, “Because.” Younger people tend to be more open to making friends, but their friendships are often shallow and brief. Older people tend to socialize less with potential friends, but their friendships may accumulate and last for years. IMHO, of course.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: It bothers me when family and friends that I invite to my home, don't invite me to their home. I know they have excuses, but it prolongs the mismatch. How do you handle it in your own life?
Answer: Let me start by saying, every large “family of families” that sticks together through a generation or two has someone or more who provide the glue for the sticking. They are the ones who make the arrangements for it to happen. They are also the ones whose hospitality makes memorable, those times. And, they will be the ones most remembered and missed by the largest attendance at their funerals. Think on that. In our extended family of about 40 who will attend a get-together at Easter, Thanksgiving, and Christmas, we have one family who graciously hosts us in their small home. It is our branch of the family’s ancestral home and we’ll bring more than enough food, drinks, ice, paper goods and utensils, etc., and folding chairs. Outside are a basketball goal and usually a volleyball net while inside are the conversationalists and ESPN lovers in the living room. When the crowd thins out after about 4–5 hours, whoever is left helps in the general cleanup and putting back folding chairs in the attic. Usually in August, my wife and I will host a get-together at our rural home in the National Forest. Our living room holds six recliners, a table for four and a big screen. The dining room will seat ten but most will bask outside in the shade or go fishing or swimming in our lake. I’ll usually grill burgers and such, and lots of folks bring food, drinks, ice, and picnic tableware. Freezers of homemade ice cream (my wife’s speciality are peach and Butterfinger) will join other desserts. That’s how we handle it. And by the way, everybody hugs everybody coming and going because we love each other and glad for the get-together.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why would someone who was friends with you and wasn't very nice to you, years later get someone to ask if you wanna meet up with them and their friend?
Answer: When it happened to me, I had moved from that area and had not seen nor heard from him in over 15 years. And, I can add, I hadn’t thought about or missed him at all. He had been instrumental in having me kicked out of where I was living and turned some friends against me. I almost lost my job. And whenever he happened to be around, he always offered some snarky better-than-me remarks. Fast-forward fifteen years, and I had become a Christian pastor and was serving two churches 300 miles away. He called on the phone and immediately started like we were long-time close friends and he wes really excited to finally be reunited. Then his pitch shifted and his goal was for me to join his multi-level marketing scheme. I had tried two of them before and I lost money both times, and I also didn’t want to waste my time and money into selling cleaning supplies. He had the gall to encourage me to use my church congregations as a ready source of customers and suckers for my credibility. When I finally made it clear that I wasn’t interested, he started unloading his sh!t-wagon on me in the same old snarky insults from years before and how stupid I was to not help him out and get rich with him. I finally interrupted him to wish him well in his business and good-bye. I haven’t heard from him since, thankfully.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Who’s someone you know who’s excellent at holding a conversation ?
Answer: Well, the Annabel James who answers your question, looks like someone who would hold your attention.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is it okay to text a friend that I don't hang out with anymore every once in a while?
Answer: Yes, it’s okay. It maintains the connection if they decide they want to renew your friendship.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is the name of your childhood friend at present who is alive?
Answer: That’s an easy one. His initials are A.G. and he is like me, a semi-retired church pastor in another state.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What do people do for fun when they're with friends? I don't understand the concept of "hanging out". I don't really have that much fun with friends and it's awkward
Answer: Most of the time, when peeps hang out in my circle and generation (Baby Boomers) we’re either talking about something we’re interested in or we’re doing something we’re interested in. I’m a church pastor, and for some number of years it could be said if I wasn’t at home I was with my best buddy pastor, and the reverse was true for him. For another number of years, I was not only a pastor, but I was also a volunteer firefighter and I was involved in all of that with other smoke-eaters. Get together with some who like bowling, putt-putt golf, tennis, pickleball, fishing or something else that interests you and your friends.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is the term for someone who has been betrayed by their best friend?
Answer: A Victim. And if they accept the “I’m sorry and I won’t do it again,” the victim has no excuse for downgrading to Stupid Victim.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What should I do if my friend steals my work but doesn't admit to it (school, buying everything I have)?
Answer: A thief is dishonest in every way. You know that she not only steals your work but she lies also. You should block her and have nothing to do with her. No talk, no sit close to her, no favors, no rides, no borrowing or loans, and certainly no forgiveness when she comes whining “I’m sorry, I won’t do it again.” She is NOT a friend — she’s a crook, a predator who takes advantage of other people’s kind nature and if you let her, she won’t learn any lesson about the consequences of dishonesty.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is an invisible friend called?
Answer: Most of mine in my childhood were other “actors” in my fantasy play. If taken too seriously nowadays it’s called a Split Personality, but I think Alter Ego is nicer. “Harvey” was the name of both the movie (1950) and the 6-feet tall invisible rabbit co-star.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How often do people my age socialise? I'm 22 and trying to improve my social life. I spend most of my free time at home watching TV and have 1 friend I rarely see. What’s a normal amount of socialising for ppl my age, and what do people usually do?
Answer: When I was 22 in 1970, I sometimes rode a motorcycle and I had a couple of friends who also did. Mostly I hung out at a public swimming pool in the summer days and a roller-skating rink when I wasn’t working for spending money. I traded some work for free admission at both places. I socialized a lot at both the pool and the rink, and I dated a lot elsewhere too.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Think about a friend who has a positive influence on you. What kind of positive things did you learn from this friend?
Answer: I learned that Christianity (following Jesus’ example and teaching) is a lot better than just sitting in church on Sunday mornings.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: This is not a question, but could share some things about feeling lonely? It’s the end of the year and my classmates are just hanging out, but I am stupid so I have no friends.
Answer: We don’t use the word “stupid” around our family. We have two members who are autistic and neither is stupid. They are gifted differently in some ways. You may be too. I never socialized with my fellow students outside of school. I socialized with the girls at the swimming pool, the roller-skating rink, the miniature golf course and places like that. And when I wasn’t just socializing, I was usually working in one of those places in exchange for free admission or as a busboy for part-time pay in a restaurant. I made friends in all of those places. Find places where your peers hang out. Don’t limit yourself to your classmates. Make friends with others in other places.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I don't have a future because I don't have a social life or friends. Is that good?
Answer: There is no necessary correlation between the two.You can still have all three: future, social life, and friends. Get off your duff and go live it.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Could my friend’s closeness with one of her ex-teachers make him uncomfortable as she calls him quite a bit to catch up wanting to organize meetups with him? She sees him as more than a teacher like a parent?
Answer: I’m not a teacher who teaches whole different classes each year in schools, but I’m a church pastor who has served fifteen churches in thirty years, almost always two at a time. When I have been appointed to different churches, I’m required to leave my former congregations behind to be served by another pastor. Sometimes someone has gotten attached and wants to hang on to me. That’s not fair to the new congregation members. It’s not fair to the classes her teacher has now, and her relationship with him is against the rules of the school system. Yes, it should make him uncomfortable.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is the biggest friendship lesson you’ve learned as an adult?
Answer: Even after being best friends for most of their lifetimes, one can make a mistake the other won’t accept an apology for and forgive, and the other may end all contact. The effect on the one is grief, as if a much-loved spouse suddenly died, and the sense of loss never goes away completely.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How does the concept of friendship evolve across different life stages, from childhood to adolescence, adulthood, and beyond?
Answer: Somebody who’s fun to be with, works across the ages. The concept of ‘fun’ can cover a variety of interactions. Practice Zen.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can I reduce the amount of time think about someone? I am friends with someone online and want to be, however, I think about them way too much. I message them and expect an answer right away whereas other friends I can wait days more detail below
Answer: I read your question, comment and more. It’s called a crush. It doesn’t have to be male or female. A crush is affection then desire raised to obsession with someone. The cure is to immerse yourself in something else you really enjoy doing to do, preferably with your brain and eyes. Just do things that you enjoy and which require your undivided attention.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Normally, I have a body temp of 98.0- 99.0 F. Lately, it’s been 100.0 or 97.0 more or less. Is that bad? What should I do?
Answer: My usual body temp is 97.4 F, but I’ve experienced the range from 96.1 - 98.4 F, so we prove that 98.6 is just somebody’s calculated average. I wouldn’t worry about it, imho.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I not get stuck with friendship problems and focus on my studies?
Answer: The easiest way to not get stuck with friendship problems is to not have supposedly friends who cause them.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I create a social environment? How do I make new friends?
Answer: Talk to people and share interests. Smile and make eye contact; honestly compliment them if you can. Be friendly to make friends that help each other. Be cheerful and have fun. Treat others equally as you would like to be treated.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I behave from now on with a member of my social group who recently hurt me by cancelling last minute in order to meet with someone else (who is also in the group and I'm not in good terms with?).
Answer: Start by forgetting the snobish “friends/social group” game. Other students are either real friends one-on-one with you or they aren’t. It’s up to you with whom you want to be real friends, so do what YOU want. I didn’t know 90% of the students when I started attending the combined high school, but I made a point of learning everybody’s names. I never rose to the socially elite level of Mister/Miss Best of anything. I was just one of the loner nerds, geeks and faces in the crowd, but I knew everybody and they knew me, and I never lacked for somebody to hang out with. But you can’t do that now because you’re limited to a few acquaintances chosen by somebody else to be their gang. Once you quit that and when you graduate, you’ll have so many opportunities for friendship that you’ll forget playing the stupid social group game. P.S. And off-campus, I had an active social life. I traded a little work at the local roller-skating rink, putt-putt miniature golf and the public swimming pool in exchange for free admission when I wasn’t working part-time for spending money in a restaurant. I raced go-karts and water-skied with friends and in all of those activities I made different friends.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Am I bad for reacting after my friends who invited me to play games told me to leave the party because the other friend's gf wants to join? I immediately left and unfriended them and unfollowed them in all social media platforms.
Answer: You repaid evil with evil, and I think that you overreacted. Now you have no friends. You’re bad to yourself.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why does my friend only ask to hang out when they know I am busy?
Answer: Maybe it’s because it’s their best time to hang out and they forget that it’s not so much for you.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can I get rid of my loneliness with my friends that leave me out of conversations? I haven’t had a true friend since middle school (Right now I’m a senior that is ready to graduate), but now I can’t seem to make any friends.
Answer: Take heart, you’re about to escape being penned-up with the cliques, “friends” groups (organized bully followers), brats and bullies and limited opportunities to make new and better friends than you’ve been stuck with. Your opportunities for making friends is about to open up. Enjoy yourself!

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Should I move back to where I used to live? Tired of not having friends and I had filled out an online application for housing, now its my turn on the waiting list and someone called me. I have a lot of friends where I used to live and should I move?
Answer: I think it could ultimately be a good move for you, if you can afford it. But you need to remember that while you were gone, some things have changed. Your friends filled their IRL friend-gaps when you left, with other friends. You will need to assimilate into the community again. And, there might be new friendships for you with even more new poeple.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why would a friend for whom you spent a lot of time and effort comforting when they had emotional problems show no interest in helping you when you are in need?
Answer: Is it possible that your time and effort comforting your friend isn’t equal to what you’re asking of your friend? I’ve seen a number of times that payback for some companionship and comforting is asked for in significant monetary terms. Your friend may not be able to help you now or may have failed to receive payback for a cash loan and be unable to donate to you what you ask. It can also mean that your friend simply isn’t as supportive as you are.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I become successful at maintaining friendships?
Answer: By maintaining them, of course, Silly! Invest time in contacting them. Be interested in their lives, and include them in your activities and social circle whenever possible. Share your resources with them on par with how they share with you. Living close enough to each other to frequently be physically present together is a major factor in maintaining friendships. Likewise, any time one friend moves into a new situation more distant is likely to be a major factor in declining friendship quality and requires more effort to maintain.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Have you ever been in public and started a conversation with someone you didn’t know ?
Answer: Sure, I do it often. Standing in line, at the gasoline pump, anytime someone catches my eye, if we’re meeting in an aisle, other spectators at the ballfield, and any place else where I feel a greeting or a compliment might lead to a friendly chat. My wife started asking me who I was talking to and I’d usually have to answer that I didn’t know them and we didn’t exchange names. I told her how I opened the conversations and now she does it also. It’s a nice way to pass the time and let people know they are worthy to not be strangers.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is having a fake friend worse than having a enemy?
Answer: Yes. You would be more open about your money and secrets with a fake friend. You wouldn’t do so to a known enemy.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I have a friend who lives in Nigeria. I have helped him before, but it is becoming a need every month. Should I continue to support him?
Answer: NO. Tell him that while you might be rich by his standards, but you have costs of living in American society and they have almost doubled in some cases. You simply cannot send him any more help. He will almost certainly up the drama of his needs and crisises he is suffering. Tell him you are sorry but you can’t send any more help, and if he ever asks again, you will end the friendship by blocking him. And do it.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Imagine when they tell you that the main reason of your down fall is your best friend. How will you feel about that?
Answer: If it had happened, I’d feel surprised and betrayed. It’s never happened and I can’t imagine any of my close friends doing that or a circumstance that could be my “downfall.”

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I get friends attention to apologize? They have been ignoring my existence for 2 weeks now.
Answer: They may be so ashamed they cannot face you. OR, they may not apologize and think you should, or at least kiss-up to them. Find new, better friends.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What should I do? Am I a toxic person if I don't trust people easily and doubt them? Should I cut off my friends just because they make me overthink when they are around me?
Answer: I wouldn’t call it ‘toxic.’ Maybe you’re afraid to trust them until you get to know them better. If it goes beyond that, you may suffer from paranoia, It sounds like you’re overly sensitive and unaware of the art of slang and harmless teasing. Perhaps you can concentrate on trusting one who appears trust-worthy until you reach your comfort level before sharing more deeply. However, your cautious approach to making friends may also protect you from getting cloned, scammed or catfished.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is it possible to find a loving and caring best friend online?
Answer: Sure, everything is possible. However, be very careful about providing too much information or pictures, and remember that they have a lot more going on than just corresponding with you.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: After years, my best friend removed me last night. She said she had a lot of pent up rage against me, and she seems to really hate me… I cared A LOT for her, but it seems it wasn't reciprocal. I'm 17. I'm completely defeated. I need to cope. How?
Answer: Breakups happen, and maybe it’s for the best that your ex-BF got out of your life. Start now by remembering that you’re not dying of old age at 17 years-old, so you have plenty of time to make better friends and leave your former BF behind. Understand that friendships at your age are most often shallow and short, and now that you’ve experienced that, you should be more careful about not having more friends to keep from getting hurt by one friendship failing.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What is your opinion on stores that have a no weapons allowed sign on the door?
Answer: I have a CCW in a state that doesn’t require one anymore. My EDC is widely acknowledged to be the smallest practical (and therefore best concealable) firearm for personal defense. Most importantly, the last thing I want is to shoot somebody. In forty years of packing heat, I’ve had about a dozen occasions when the simple display of my weapon (called ‘Brandishing’) stopped a potential violsnt felony. I plan on carrying my weapon everyplace I know. I regularly walk into banks and government offices, restaurants that serve alcohol; old friends from the old days and the churches I’ve pastored and now am serving in the recent thirty-odd years. I even attend school and recreational sporting events and chat up the cops (I was one and know how they think). No little sign will stop me from entering any of those prohibited-weapons places, because the defenseless are obvious prey for the evil people. I’m not trying to do the cop’s job. I’m just trying to prepare a defense.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: My best friend and I keep fighting over small things. Am I in the wrong, or is she?
Answer: You are both in the wrong. Next time, flip a coin to decide which one wins and gracefully accept your victory or your defeat.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I asked my friend who is 70 if she ever owned a credit card. She said, "Of course." Is this normal?
Answer: In the 1960’s USA, some of the higher-class department stores offered credit cards which could only be used there. I can remember once in the 1970’s, Mastercard mass-mailed credit cards to thousands of people who had never applied for one. Many of those who received one, used it without any idea about what “credit” was — until the bills rolled in and they were deep in debt! I married in 1976 and my wife and I applied for a Mastercard in ’77 to help us smooth out the payments on purchases we made for a television and furniture. The company we worked for paid us twice monthly and the credit card kept us from struggling in-between. Lots of my generation (I’m 75) have had a credit card at one time or another. The danger comes when the amount owed is more than one can be paid off.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Are you your child’s friend?
Answer: Both of our sons are now adults in their 40’s. They lived with us into their 20’s and were making adult decisions before they moved out on their own. We are all self-supporting adults and we associate as best friends with family love. They have families, one with teenagers and one with grown children, and while they occasionally ask what we think about something, we only offer our opinions and not orders to perform. Yes, we’re best friends.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What can I write about (my best friend's personality)?
Answer: The organization of the Boy Scouts of America’s “Scout Law” says the scouts should be: “Trustworthy, Loyal, Helpful, Friendly, Courteous, Kind, Obedient, Cheerful, Friendly, Brave, Clean, and Reverent.” Hopefully your BF has these qualities.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What should you do when you're just giving in a friendship and not getting anything back?
Answer: That’s called “buying friendship.” The real problem is that anyone who requires you to reward them for hanging around, are not friends at all. Stop making the payments and they’ll disappear. Then find new friends who have a sense of fairness.

Name: Joe Lawson

Question: How do real-world applications of interpersonal skills, learned in class and through experiences, ready students for success beyond academics, including navigating social dynamics, networking, and adapting to diverse contexts?
Answer: Immeasurably. I majored in business administration and management and throughout my life (I’m 75 and still working part-time), I’ve worked with people. I’ve worked in restaurants, retail stores, factories, convenience stores and I’ve been self-employed. I’ve been a deputy sheriff, a bouncer in a roadhouse, a firefighter, industrial engineer, carpenter, school bus driver, sawyer in a mill, cook and cashier, several kinds of clerk and a few less mentionable occupations, and for the last 33 years, a God-called Methodist church pastor. A local couple who were lifelong members of a different denomination church, started attending one of the churches I served. When I asked them why, they said their current pastor couldn’t relate with them. He was a fresh doctorate who couldn’t understand the everyday problems and relational issues they caused, because, they said, all he knew was what was in books. I had real-world knowledge of life and dealing with others. I can and often do, start and have conversations with total strangers in public, just for the fun of a chat. (My wife finally asked me how and now she does it too.) My point is that if you want someone to do something, you have to relate with them. As for books, I recommend “Games People Play” by Eric Berne (Transactional Analysis), and “Generation to Generation” by Edwin H. Friedman (relationships).

Question: As a cop, what's the best excuse given from someone speeding that turned out to be true?

Question: If you have friends that don't take the time out to see you or even talk to you, should you still keep them in your life?

Question: If a cop pulls you over and says, "You did not fully stop at the stop sign", what should you say in response? Perhaps, "Officer, I have a right to see video evidence of this accusation"? Or is that actually a terrible response?

Question: Is it possible for non-Catholics to attend mass with their Catholic friends or family members?

Question: What would you say if your elderly friend really shouldn't be driving anymore as she's careless and I think has dementia, but always picks you up once a month to take you to her house for dinner? Would be very angry if I told her the truth.

Question: As an introvert, while in public have you ever started a conversation with someone you didn’t know without having an agenda behind it ?

Question: Is it rude to give a friend clothing/items and tell them they can do whatever they want with, only to turn around a few weeks later and ask for the clothing/items back when you see they have them for sale on social media? How would you handle it?

Question: My boss did not inform me of his incoming visitors from abroad until the morning of their arrival. He wants me to stay with them for weeks in my apartment. What do I do? I am scared.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Have you ever had a friend just completely ruin something for you? Plz share so I don’t feel as depressed.
Answer: About 2 years ago, my longtime best friend blocked me out of his life. We live more than a day’s drive apart since he moved 5 years ago, but we regularly talked an hour or more every week on the phone. We had shared interests throughout our decades-long friendship and always had something to talk about. All gone. I’ve grieved my loss, meanwhile easily spending those hours doing something else. I looked at our relationship and how he had regularly moved some distance every 5–10 years. He greeted everybody with “Hi Guy (Gal) and I had become either “Man” or “Dude” in all other remarks. I realize now that he had a record of changing homes and friendships without much concern and I had just hung on long too long. I occasionally see a picture or something which triggers a thought about him, but I’m over it.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can you be a friend and also let them know your status?

Question: I made a new friend but started gradually distancing when she started treating me badly. She went ballistic on me and badmouthed me to common acquaintances. How could I have prevented a scandal?

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How good are you at getting along with others ?

Question: This person always pesters me with these topics that are bothering me. He knows I don't want to talk about them. He doesn't talk about it with others, only me. Why does he only need to talk about it with me?

On the other hand… Quora was designed to gather the knowledge of things learned by men and women which aren’t normally found in libraries. Our answers are supposed to offer a fact or opinion and then some support for that reasoning. Some of us are a little lazy about supporting what we claim as the truth and just toss a flip remark at the Original Poster’s question. The person who pesters you may just like your “Yeah, who cares? … He doesn’t… No .. Mudsharks” unsupported style of pronounced answers. He’s learning to talk like you, and he will be bothered just as much when someone presses him to justify what he has said, as you are now with him.

Question: Today when my friends and I were walking we were suddenly surrounded by 8 thieves and I ran away from my friends and was I right?

Stewardesses on airline flights instruct the passengers that in case of an in-flight emergency and the air masks drop down, they should put their own on first before trying to help others with theirs. Firefighters may act carelessly around fires, but I was taught as a fireman, “Never walk into a fire that you aren’t certain you can walk out of.” I won’t do it again. Always be sure you can save yourself before you try saving others in an apparently hopeless situation.

Question: If someone doesnt want anyone to become their best friend, so what is it really like is it bad or good, like the person treats everyone equally and doesn't want anyone specific to know all about them excluding their life partner?

Question: Why do authentically honest and kind people never have any real friends?

Question: Is shyness and being quiet always a sign of social anxiety, or could it be a characteristic of introversion?

Question: How can a friendship end over a frivolous thing that can tear friends apart?
Answer: How frivolous/fun versus how insulting/condemning/ridiculing/embarrassing the thing was, was understood widely different in the minds of the frivolous doer and the unsuspecting victim. Being “innocently mean” to someone who was considered an easy target and believing that the doer has so little concern for the victim’s feelings has split many friendships. It could have been because the victim was already upset over previous things done to them and the frivolous thing was just the most recent incident of being “picked on” that made the victim decide to quit the pain by quitting the relationship. And sometimes, no amount of “excuses for apologies” like “I’m sorry, I didn’t know,” or “But it was so funny” just make the breakup instant and permanent. Be careful with your frivolity, because it’s not always funny to the victim.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Does the desire to meet new people fade away more and more as a person gets older, is it normal to still want to be meet new people when your older ?
Answer: I believe it depends on the older person’s memory capabilities. For example, people suffering from Alzheimer’s often lose their most recent memories first, making it difficult for them to remember names and faces. In her last months, my late mother-in-law referred to her daughters as “the one who cuts my fingernails and toenails” and “the woman who fixes my hair, and her oldest son as either her husband or brother more often than her son. Meanwhile, she never forgot my name or our sons’ names. The difficulty and embarrassment at their condition makes some older folks reluctant to even try to meet and remember new names and faces. I’m 76yo and I’m grateful that my beloved wife can remember everybody’s names and help me on names of some people I haven’t seen in years.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I tell my friend that her everyday drinking is ruining our friendship? She’s competitive while insulting girls, self-destructive, bashing her appearance, life, and family trauma. It’s too much and I’ve spoken to her about my concern. Now what?
Answer: You can tell your friend that you love her and are concerned about her well-being and your shared relationship. You can ask her to please stop using alcohol to forget her problems. Alcoholics and drug users are “doctoring* themselves” by self-medicating to avoid coping with their real-life problems. *D.O.C.T.O.R. here means Drug Of Choice To Overcome Reality. Until the unpleasant reality is dealt with, the users will not stop self-medicating. Trust me on this, the voice of a recovering alcoholic and drug addict. And almost always, the user won’t stop doctoring themselves until they “hit rock-bottom.” That is when they either die, or they are facing a greater perceived loss like becoming homeless, divorce and losing a beloved family, They-the-user absolutely has to make the rock-bottom decision that only they can say “Stop.” Every attempt to protect them from hitting rock-bottom just prolongs their thinking they don’t have to quit using their drug.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why do some people claim to have no friends but still have a large social circle? Is this statement true or do they actually have friends?
Answer: “Friends” is a rather flexible term for others you know besides family. I’m a church pastor, and I have met and been in company with literally thousands of people in my life. Some became friends while I served in their churches, and besides church attendance we did the things friends do to help each other. Friends usually can maintain contact with each other even if they don’t live close enough to exchange help or do things together. I also came to become acquainted with many others in those communities. We knew each other’s names, family members, phone numbers, etc., saw each other once or more times a month and were friendly with each other in social settings. Such people are often loosely called ‘friends’ because they can become more useful to us, but they are actually ‘acquaintances.’ Either way, friends and acquaintances are both included in social circles, but the strength of our connections with friends is greater than that of acquaintances because friends help each other and that adds time, whereas acquaintances are usually helpful briefly and simply.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do you deal with your adult child living at home and not contributing anything financially but taking from the household?
Answer: We didn’t have the problem. Our older son accepted a position before graduating college and has risen through the ranks at that employer. That’s plenty of time for THEM to find a job and a place to live. In the meantime, save up so you can cover the rental deposit. If possible, get a dependable used car for their transportation (AND HOME IF THEY DON’T FIND A JOB TO PAY RENT, TELL THEM THAT). And stick to it. Most bums know that the gravy train has to stop sometime. Go ahead and kick them out with police help if necessary. Six months.

Question: I have two coworkers who are friends. I started ignoring one of them because I want the other one to ask me about the other coworker. My plan did not work. Why?

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is it not normal to not be shy when meeting new people ?
Answer: I think it depends on one’s self-confidence in social situations. The main reason for shyness when meeting new people is fear of looking or sounding stupid when they first meet. The famous “First Impression Is Everything” is more correctly “The first impression is important but even a goof or two is acceptable so stay calm.” I won my confidence by practicing for 15–30 minutes at a time in front of a large mirror, telling outrageous lies and dirty jokes without laughing, while striving to look sincere, honest and credible, looking into their/my eyes and controlling my voice to make it sound like the absolute truth. Basically, I learned how to hide my fears by controlled lying. It worked until the second or third introduction when I realized meeting new people was easier than I’d thought, and I started having fun meeting people. That was in my childhood. Nowadays if I’m standing in a line with other strangers, I’ll start a conversation that might last 5–10 minutes with a stranger and we might have a great time just chatting — and never exchanged names! It’s nice to learn how easily we can get along with others we haven’t already known.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Do you think when you are always being told nice things by your friends, they are most likely lying to you? Do you think unfortunately for us we don't choose our friends, but God chooses them for us?

I don’t think it’s unfortunate that God places people who can influence us to be God’s kind of person, somehow like Jesus. But we always have choices and making bad ones can have unfortunate consequences.

Question: Is it possible to meet new people in your later years and become extremely close friends with them as if you've known them since childhood?

Question: My 15-year old daughter wants an iPhone for her 16th birthday. Unfortunately, we can't afford an iPhone, and we tried to explain this to her. However, she is very angry and has stopped speaking to us. What should we do?
Answer: Almost certainly, your daughter doesn’t just want any old iPhone but instead, a brand new (currently) iPhone 15 Pro. She wants it — not because it has excellent photographic capabilities, but because it’s the new and expensive status symbol among teenagers who aren’t asking for a new car. I suggest that if you can, you offer her an iPhone 11, which is two models earlier and is close to an iP15 in performance. If you can’t make that work, you might offer her a loan after she gets a job that can handle the bill on an iPhone 15. She’s old enough to learn that living large requires giving work. Please don’t let her miss this lesson. When our sons reached driving age, one got a 25 year-old pickup that needed repairs and the other got my old car. They used them to get to work to make money for things they wanted. They took pride in being able to earn things instead of begging for gifts. Excuse me for sounding a little archaic, but I was hustling for paying, part-time jobs when I was 12 and I had to get my Social Security card when I was 14 years old. My parents told me that if I wanted money and the things it could buy, all I had to do was be willing to work and somebody would pay me for it. I had a part-time job for money, and I also exchanged work for free admission at the nearby skating rink and public swimming pools. Now I’m 75 years old, my wife is 70 and we are semi-retired but work a couple of days per week to stay active. Our older son expects to retire a multi-millionaire at 55 yo, and our younger son is semi-retired at 44.

Question: My fiancé says it isn’t cruel to kick one’s child out of the house on their eighteenth birthday, for no other reason than, “They are now an adult, and they have to be reliant on themselves.” Is this true?
Answer: I know several families where parents told their teenagers they would be “on their own when they turned eighteen.” It wasn’t a spur-of-the-moment-at-18 announcement, and all had a job and were helped with the financial adjustments of deposits, down payments and furnishings. They were successful. I also know of others who let their legally-adult children loaf around the house while not finding a job, completing schooling or contributing to their own upkeep. Their overage children had “failure to launch” and some failed to accomplish more than being dependent on others or drugs. Now, here’s my approach. We have two sons. We taught them that they never had to lie, cheat or steal to get money. All they had to do was be willing to work and somebody would pay them for it. Our home was heated with burning wood and starting as pre-schoolers, they earned a penny per small pine cone and two pennies for large ones to kindle fires in the heater. The older son lived with us until he graduated college at 22. He worked in maintenance and house painting before graduating, and after, where he is still employed in his 40’s with a six-figure salary. The younger son lived with us until he was 21, working in a paint store and then in construction before enlisting in the USAF. He retired at 42 and was immediately employed as a part-time civilian contractor, and he also has a six-figure income. There is great satisfaction to be gained when we are self-supporting adults, and great comfort and pride in having self-supporting adult children.

Question: Can it be true that new friends may be poems, but old friends are alphabets, do not forget the alphabets, because you will need them to read the poems?
Answer: To a person who knows nothing about mountains, all mountains are just mountains. To a person who knows very little about mountains, all mountains are different. To a person who knows everything about mountains, all mountains are just mountains. Zen.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Can a police officer take your firearm and unload it if you have a concealed carry license permit?
Answer: Mississippi law has issued “carry concealed weapons” (CCW) permits since the 1990’s but modified the carry-laws to not require them and also allows unconcealed open carry without permits. However, I’ve bought the CCW permits since they began. The CCW permits are issued with the same number as one’s drivers’ license and I’m not ashamed to pack heat, so whenever I’m asked for my ID by a law enforcement officer (LEO), I hand them both. Invariably, I receive a grin and a wish to stay safe as they immediately return my cards and wave me on.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is it possible to still be friends with a school friend you haven't seen for years?
Answer: Sure it is! In fact, those who attended the 1–8 grade school when I did, have a Fb page, and those I attended high school with in 1962–1966 have a Fb page spanning 1961–1975. They meet monthly for food and fellowship and year-classes usually have five- or ten-year reunions. I reunited last year with a friend from our racing days in 1966–67 after being apart for 30+ years. My boss/office manager whom I worked for from 1973–81 called me last month to catch-up and we talked for an hour. I was a deputy sheriff in 1978–80 when our current sheriff was a state trooper and our paths seldom crossed, but nowadays we greet each other as old buddies in the blue. My point is that friends almost always have something they enjoy doing together, and they can often recall and renew their friendship.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Does being able to easily make friends help in life?
Answer: I believe that being “charming” can help to open us to potential friendships. A natural talent or accommodating behavior which “breaks the ice” between strangers or makes them more willing to share a relationship with us is almost essential in creating friendships. It is “friendliness;” the condition of openness to a genuine friend-relationship.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can a loner get friends in high school if the other loners like to be alone and don't seem to want any friends?
Answer: Your question is like many others, in that the problem of finding friends occurs in The High School. Apparently it’s a different world there now with Friends Groups and such. When I went to HS, everybody knew everybody else’s name and usually something about them. If you wanted to get to better know someone, you just sat or stood next to them and talk. But if you can’t do that… Read Stan Parkes’ answer about having fun activities. For me, school was a place that interfered with my having fun. Well, sometimes, anyway. I did those things Stan wrote about. I roller-skated, went bowling and swam in the local public pool when it was open. I had a part-time job for spending money and usually also worked in the places where I played to get free admission. At every place I went, there were people to talk to or have fun with.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Has anyone ever gotten a FB friend Request from a dead friend? (I just did.)
Answer: Yes, I’ve gotten FB friend requests supposedly from friends who have died. They are from scammers who have harvested friend lists from someone who had friended them while they were alive. And I’ve gotten repeated requests from several deceased friends, probably because nobody is managing their accounts. My Fb account shows that I have 826 “Fb friends.” Some are truly my offline friends, some are online-only friends, some I became acquainted with in spiritual growth programs like Cursillo and Walk to Emmaus, some I met who were members of churches I served, and there are some who were attracted by my theology or other interests. Nowadays when I receive Fb friend requests, I go to the applicant’s page and if it doesn’t look like a legitimate request from a real, living friend, I notify Fb that it’s a scam and delete the request.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What are you wanting to do now? Are you looking for a friend?
Answer: I WAS wanting to refill my coffee (did it) while the TV spews morning news from the big city 50 miles away. It’s full of shootings, carjackings, court cases, violent demonstrations, corrupt government and seemingly endless cases of horrible child abuse. And shortly after breakfast, I’ll go outside in the beauty and quiet of nature in the National Forest where I live. My wife and I are cutting a briar thicket and saplings in a 5-acre patch to improve our view of the lake behind our home. (Just FYI, she’s 70 y.o. and I’m 75 y.o. and we have matching tool sets including identical chainsaws!) And later today, we’ll be in Bible studies with a dozen friends and relatives.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What do you do if your close friend randomly stops speaking to you?
Answer: I would (and have done) “randomly” stop trying to speak to them and instead have my conversations with other friends while living my relatively active life. I have friends and relatives who like to stay in regular contact and some who don’t. I’ve learned to accept each of them according to their likes and dislikes. If one of them randomly puts our relationship on hold, I can always talk with my wife and two adult sons. We share interests and chat regularly. And honestly, I’m comfortable with being alone and involved in reading, in artistic hobbies, and enjoying life surrounded by nature on my property within a National Forest.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can anyone get a unique friend that we can tell him everything?
Answer: That’s easy! When two people are mutually attracted and go through a reasonable period of exploring each other’s character, they can enter into a legally-binding contract to remain friends through any and all later differences. It’s called “marriage,” and I’m in my forty-seventh year of one. It works!

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Who agrees that if you are a loser or if you fail a lot and lost your home and became homeless, it is best to cut ties with successful family and successful friends because you will drag them down to your level and thats not fair to them?
Answer: I DISAGREE. Being a Methodist pastor has brought me around homeless people. Every single one of them said their homelessness was a temporary thing. They neither wanted to be homeless nor would they suggest to anyone to join them in their poverty. You just wish they would disappear instead of reminding you, “There but for happenstance and accident, go I.”

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Would you speak up if you don’t like your significant other’s friends?
Answer: Not me, but my spouse. I have a friend from being coworkers in the mid-1980’s, and who is not on my wife’s friends list. The obvious reason is that he didn’t remember her name, and when he called on the phone and she answered, he simply said, “Let me talk to Joe.” She says that he’s rude and ill-mannered. And it’s true that he can be abrupt and lacking in the “social graces.” He was also living on the streets and supporting himself as a teenager, and sometimes on the wrong side of the law. He has a couple of bullet scars while I don’t, but both of us have been gunslingers in our past, and that’s our link. He and I agreed to care for each other’s families if something happened to us and/or them.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I don't want to talk to teachers but because of that, I have missing assignments. What should I do?
Answer: You can try what I did in the third six-weeks period of the fifth grade! Everybody kept telling me that I was really smart and I should be making better grades. I finally believed them and I decided I was so smart that I didn’t need to do homework or take tests. I thought I was SO smart that the teacher and the school should just give me straight-A’s in appreciation. But when I brought my report card home to be signed, all of my grades were marked “0” (zero}. And the next hour included a quick trip back to the school with my mother, a quick conference between her and the teacher, a quick trip back home to cut a switch and a whipping to stimulate the blood flow from my butt to my brain. I was then, smart enough to make sure I did all of my studies and assignments.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I stopped talking to my coworker and she begged me to look at her. I still talk to her friend. Why doesn't her friend seem angry with me?
Answer: Yours (and theirs) is the type of behavior to be expected from junior high and high school “mean girls” and it has no place in the grown-up world. Try growing up and getting along.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: My best friend is blackmailing me, and I also want to be best friends with him. What do I do?
Answer: Your wrongly-described your blackmailer “friend” which overrules any hope of your being best friends. You are being used by someone who has Narcissistic Abuse Disorder. Genuine friends do not blackmail you. Narcissists do that and they are very charming while they are getting their way with you, but blackmailing is forcing you to to do things for them and it will only get worse. If you don’t believe me, stop paying the blackmail and see your supposedly “best friend” become unfriendly to you. Get away from him and stay away. Block his attempts to contact you.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: My friend and I were in the car, both of us are 12, and we heard a voice saying her name at the same time, but no one else heard it. What should I do?
Answer: As a longtime Christian Pastor… in the Bible, 1 Samuel 3:11 says, “If it happens again, say “Speak, Lord, for I am listening.” That is especially true, if you were feeling close to God in the moment.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: A friend called me a pedo and my best friend had his side. What should I do?
Answer: If it’s not true and there’s no proof, then deny it as a ridiculously untrue accusation. If it’s not true and there’s no proof, neither of your so-called friends are friends at all. Don’t have anything to do with them ever again.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do you start a conversation with a new friend on Facebook?
Answer: Actually, a big share of my Fb “friends” are people I’ve been actual friends with in real life. The conversations were started long ago and were just renewed on Fb. Ask yourself why you got on Facebook (Fb). Friendship requires having shared interests and helping each other through life. So, look for Fb pages in which you have some interest. Meanwhile, Get some pictures on your page, add some information and what you can say to your new friend beyond “Hi, I’m ___. interested in favorite sports teams, musicians — get the picture?

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I disconnect you from my life?
Answer: Assuming that you mean from Quora: Neither of us are followers of the other, so…, First, try to simply think tiredly, “there again,” when you see my name and don’t dwell on it. Just move on. If that doesn’t work for you, it’s not a stretch to believe I’m catfishing, and under my totally opposite persona as a doddering old fool, I’m really a very shy but also veerrrry hot and horny lover like in your most wicked dreams. How about it, lover boy? Wouldn’t that be more fun than either of us leaving Quora?

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is it normal for me to involuntarily smile when I think about my best friend?
Answer: Yes. It’s your brain’s sign of emotional gladness at their friendship.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can an introvert stop feeling horrific when they finally pluck up the courage to speak in company, but then someone immediately talks over them and everyone looks & listens to this other person causing the introvert to stop mid-sentence?
Answer: There are ill-mannered, rude, egotistical people everywhere, and you just described one. They don’t just interrupt introverts; they interrupt any- and every-one who is talking because they simply love the sound and feeling of their own ideas gushing forth over everybody else’s. I encourage you to realize and believe that almost certainly it’s not a personal attack on you as an introvert. Learn to take a deep breath of resignation — not for your perceived sense of weakness but that your friends group allows the jerk to monopolize the conversation. If it had been me, I would have stood up looked the rude interrupter in the eyes, given the jerk the finger and left that group. That would mark your coming-out as an extrovert. There are plenty of real friends to be made elsewhere. Don’t worry about losing your so-called “company.” They sided with the wrong person, and it’s their loss.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I deal with a friend who was friends with me just to make money off of me?
Answer: Unless your real name is “Free Money,” stop letting it happen! Avoid going places with the moocher where they might obligate you to pay for or buy them something. If they want you to drive them somewhere, let them know you need fuel for your vehicle and unless they can pay, you can’t make the trip. I went through a number of so-called friends when I was a teenager who mooched money, free rides, movie tickets, fast food, cigarettes and such. It ended when I worked up the courage to demand they had to provide the food for our next trip to the lake. Imagine three teenage boys with appetites and no fast-food or concessions, and their provision was a frozen chicken stolen from their family’s freezer! They laughed and said I had only told them to bring food, and that I could cook it for them! That was the end of my providing a free ride to moochers — and they dumped me and found another sucker. Don’t be a sucker. Dump the moocher.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Should your best friend have certain qualities?
Answer: Certainly, liking you should be at the top of the list, and tied for first would be your liking them. Everything else should be truthful, honest, fair, and ability to be equals. Oh, and close proximity.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I was raised sheltered and now I don't know how to socialize and behind my peers in many aspects. Sometimes I feel like a mistake. What should I do?
Answer: You are not a mistake! You are just not as practiced in socializing. Practice talking to your family and friends — or to a large mirror for 10–15 minutes a day. You’ve been shut-up too long. It’s time for you to get better at friendly talking.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I’m thinking of going mute. Not that I'm depressed or anything, I am grateful, but what would happen if I just stop talking around friends and family?
Answer: You would be mute JUST around friends and family? Not at the restaurant to prevent you from describing what you want, or the doctor, dentist, police officer to report a crime, etc,. etc., etc.? What if your parents “mute” their setting a plate for you at mealtimes or providing you with the comforts of home? I don’t know about your family, but my parents would have a “quick, fast, and in a hurry” whipping-way to restore my voice and it would leave painful red stripes on my butt and legs. I promise that such treatment would restore your voice too. Try it and see!

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How bad am I if I kicked my best friend in the balls? Does it hurt that much? I'm a boy.
Answer: I think it will only be fair for you to let him do that to you. Yes, it hurts that much, so close your eyes when you do so you can feel why males are so protective of their testicles.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I found out that after I left my ex-best friends behind because they were fake friends that they started to make fun of me on their social media accounts. Why did they do that?
Answer: Let me offer you an example. I’m sure you know that you need to make sure your bottom is clean after you have a bowel movement. Otherwise, your rear-end will smell like you-know-what. from what we used to call “dingle-balls of excrement” left behind. Finish your “bowel movement” by getting rid of those little POS’s in your consciousness. Blocking, ignoring, avoiding their childish temper fits, and filling your life with clean, fresh friends. Finish the job of flushing them away and and go get in the living room of your life.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What if you think your friends are not your true friends?
Answer: I would probably, almost certainly, drift away from those I believed were truly not my friends.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What are some good nonviolent bullying techniques for adults? My son keeps getting in trouble for bullying his classmate, so I want to start bullying that kid’s dad.
Answer: HOW ABOUT… doing something about YOUR SON instead of your bully-son’s victim’s father? If it was MY son that YOUR son was bullying, I could almost certainly help YOUR son and HIS father keep YOU and YOUR son from getting in any more trouble.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why do I make fake arguments in my head with other people, especially with/of my friends to the point where it’s beginning to stress me out?
Answer: If your mental arguments are related to your real life relationships with them, then you’re practicing for the breakup that verbally arguing with them could cause. I remember dating a girl in our mid-teens, she was so fine, so fun, so happy. We made a great couple —until I believed a rumor that she wanted to break up with me. My teen male ego couldn’t bear that. I practiced my argument, went to her house, and broke up with her first. Then she told me the rumor was all wrong and she wanted us to stay together. Again, my ego couldn’t admit my mistake, and I turned and walked away. Stop practicing for the breakup. Look at everyone for their good qualities and be glad you have good friends!

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Who agrees by staying in your lane and hanging out with people in your league? Do you think you will be happier because you are hanging around with people that have more in common with you?
Answer: I believe we all have a comfort zone when we are surrounded by those like ourselves. I do. But more than once, I’ve really surprised friends who then ask me, “How do you know these people?!” Sometimes it’s because “these people” are well known, popular, highly regarded or just obviously above whomever they might normally expect. But again, there’s always a connection between us.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How can one get over the hurt caused in friendship on both sides? When you both hurted each other a lot unintentionally but you want to stay friends even if the hurt cut really deep. How can one know If its possible to recover the friendship?
Answer: Forgive each other. Forget the hurt and never dwell on it.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: My 23-year-old son got a DUI last night and is asking for me to help financially. I can but I want him to learn his lesson. What should I do?
Answer: Ask him what is in it for you. You are rightfully hurt emotionally by his failure in judgment. He will not learn anything about actions having consequences and bad actions with bad consequences, if you simply bail him out financially. Be sure that a part of his repayment is to participate in a safe-driving course or a series of Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) meetings.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I have no friends despite talking to lots of people, having fun with them, and asking them questions. Everyone sees me as an acquaintance. What is wrong with me?
Answer: Nothing is wrong with you OR them. You all are acquaintances — know each other’s names, something about them and talk to each other. All of that is just normal social pastimes. You were in a crowd with them and that was it. Nobody actually helped anybody so there are no favors, no kindnesses to repay to attach you to anyone, and no time together while you share a common interest more deeply. The first two stanzas of the Christian “The Servant Song” say, “Will you let me be your servant, Let me be as Christ to you; Pray that I may have the grace to Let you be my servant, too. We are pilgrims on a journey, We are travelers on the road; We are here to help each other, Walk the mile and bear the load.” You have to do something with someone to reach the time to share more deeply with an individual and open up to each other.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: What are some good ways to make friends with people who are older than you when you are a young adult (in your early twenties)?
Answer: Many of us oldsters (I’m 75) joke about still being an 18 yo on the inside wondering what the heck happened. We remember our good and bad experiences and what we learned from them. If we start talking about them, it’s to lead up to what we learned that might serve as an encouragement or a warning to a younger person. Please be patient while we try to describe it. Becoming friends with anyone of any age requires that you and they share an interest and can help each other to “get where they’re going” in life. For example, I encouraged one of our sons to become an engineer because he had the personality for it. He made friends with two retired engineers who helped him through college while he helped them with painting and repairs.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Can a person be genuinely good but struggle to make friends due to their introverted personality?
Answer: Sure! The issue of a person being an introvert or an extrovert doesn’t have any relationship with whether they are morally good or bad persons.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Is it possible for a person to never be shy at all in their life, even when they were a kid ?
Answer: I believe so. I can’t recall ever having been shy. In fact, I can’t remember ever being completely without friends. I remember preschool playmates before attending public school and I have memories of being involved with other friends in every grade. I grew up in my parent’s restaurant and was always involved with their employees, and I worked there and related with the customers. Even when I wasn’t at work there, I traded work for free admission to the nearby public swimming pool in the summer and year-round at a skating rink. While I do enjoy quiet time alone, I’m also a lifelong extrovert and have been in some form of management or teamwork in the few years when I haven’t been preaching every week as a full-time church pastor. And now, my hobby time is mostly spent relating with people by writing on the Internet, here and for the owner. I have personal online content with over 3 million views, and that ain’t shy.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Where can I meet some friends?
Answer: You can MEET with some of the friends you have MADE almost anywhere. You can also MAKE friends almost anywhere you can MEET strangers — workplaces, play-places, at school, in businesses and any other places congregate. You just have to be friendly enough to “break the ice” between strangers with a conversation, introduction or other reaching out.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: If I was put in a large group of people, say for instance at a school, I would pick 2 or 3 people to hang out with for the rest of the year and not get close to anyone else. Is this normal?
Answer: Normal isn’t deliberately picking 2 or 3 people out of a crowd on the first day — as it sounds like in your wording. How would you be assured those few would want to be friends with you? And it excludes others who might like you as time goes along. I believe it’s more likely that faced with a crowd, you get acquainted with a few people and you and they like having each other around, and you become friends of some sort. Meanwhile, other people are doing the same thing. Hopefully pretty soon, everybody will have found someone to be friends with. And here’s the thing about friendships. They require time spent on being friendly, and the amount of time spent on our friends means less time to meet others to become friends with them. We might become well-enough acquainted with others to learn their names and something about them, but get no closer than that.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I'm an authoritarian. Why does everyone dislike me?
Answer: An authoritarian acts like a boss. Spelled backwards, “boss” reads “double SOB.” Understand?

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Do you think if someone bullies you, you need to ask them what you did to them for them to treat you in a bad way and also ask how can I get you to respect me? Do you think we need to become friends with the people who bullied us eventually?
Answer: No, I failed to ever get bullies to respect me on those terms. I found other ways that they understood to get respect.
